correctness.rationale: The two graph presentations on Z_4^2 are checked to be 6-regular with exactly two common neighbors per distinct vertex pair, and their vertex links distinguish them. The even-scale intrinsic Čech formula in Adams–Shukla–Singh Lemma 2.2 identifies maximal faces exactly as closed neighborhoods. From 16 explicit seven-vertex facets, the exhaustive enumerations give Shrikhande f-vector (16,120,400,512,336,112,16), rook (16,120,464,536,336,112,16). Deterministic Morse pairings match 744 / 768 pairs, leaving one critical 0-cell and 23 / 63 critical 2-cells. For every face inclusion of codimension one, the script forms the appropriately reversed Hasse arc and exhaustively topologically sorts all 5952 / 6240 arcs; these are actual acyclic matchings, not unverified greedy heuristics. Forman then yields a CW model with one 0-cell and only 2-cells, so all attachments are constant and the exact integral homotopy types are wedges of 23 / 63 two-spheres. Independent GF(2) rank computations give ranks (15,105,272,240,96,16) / (15,105,296,240,96,16). The exhaustive finite computations and the classical two-graph classification jointly support the universal quantifier; no extrapolation from partial sampling is made. Both complexes are pure dimension six and have nonzero reduced second homology, ruling out shellability.

originality.rationale: The accepted new content is the exact Shrikhande scale-two closed-ball Čech homotopy type, combined with the separately cited classical two-graph parameter classification and Matsushita’s already-published rook-graph computation. Adams–Shukla–Singh provide the construction but analyze hypercubes. The directly inspected Matsushita Example 3.5 proves rook, not Shrikhande. Previte’s equivalent distance-neighborhood complexes include other graphs. Neither clique-complex nor Lovász open-neighborhood statements imply a closed-ball Shrikhande result. Searches did not identify an exact equivalent, without being treated as proof of exhaustive novelty.
residual_risks: An unpublished, inaccessible or unindexed earlier equivalent Shrikhande Čech computation may exist; absence from searched indexed literature is not proof of novelty.
The classical strongly regular graph classification is imported from literature and not independently re-proved.

value.rationale: The unique exceptional pair of nonisomorphic strongly regular graphs with identical parameters and spectrum presents a mathematically natural test of whether an intrinsic topological graph invariant is parameter-determined. A full exact homotopy type for the Shrikhande graph fills the missing member of this two-type classification, and its 23-dimensional reduced H_2 contrasts sharply with the published rook 63-dimensional H_2. The exact CW reduction and non-shellability are constructive structural results, not an arbitrary small numeric slice. The result does not claim a general classification beyond this exceptional parameter set.
